builderInsights.title: Aaron Levie
builderInsights.suggestedTitle: 企业需要的是 token 预算，不只是 headcount
builderInsights.suggestedSummary: 随着 agent 开始承担更长周期的工作，token 预算会变成真正的企业规划问题。它更像是在管 headcount、marketing spend，或者午餐预算，而不是传统的 IT 成本。Aaron Levie 认为，企业会需要新的 software 和新的 control，把 compute 分配给最有价值的工作。这甚至可能催生出一个全新的 startup 类别。

tweets.text:
A common trend emerging in larger enterprises is token budgeting as a major topic. As agents can do more and more long running tasks, and thus take vastly more compute, allocation of tokens across teams becomes a very real thing in the enterprise.

Companies spend a meaningful amount of time deciding how much to spend on talent, marketing campaigns, events, laptop setups, and even the cost of lunches. Tokens will be no different.

Tokens will similarly need to be excruciatingly well-managed because you’ll need to ensure you don’t blow up your budget, and you’ll need to ensure that the tokens are flowing to the highest and most useful parts of work. You don’t want to find out you burned your monthly budget on something relatively low value and then be blocked on the much higher value task later. 

Doing this at large company scale is extremely hard as you have layers of abstraction on data and visibility into the digital work being done by agents in any central way. This is going to mean that agentic spend will increasingly will expand beyond the confines of the IT budget, and end up in organizational budgets like other expenses. 

Ultimately team and org leaders will have to be given budgets for this, but even they don’t have adequate visibility and controls in most cases. We’ll need all new software just to solve this problem, and it’s probably an opportunity for startups in its own right.

Going to be an all new era of enterprise resource allocation, especially while we compute constrained.

podcastHighlights.title: Claude 平台的秘密：来自打造它的团队
podcastHighlights.suggestedTitle: Claude 的 platform 正在变成 agent infrastructure layer，而不只是一个 API
podcastHighlights.suggestedSummary:
**核心结论：** Claude 的 platform 正在从“model access”转向一整套能快速落地 autonomous agents 的 full stack。

- 真正的产品早就不只是一个 completion endpoint 了；而是一组带明确观点的 primitives，帮 Claude 用更少的工作拿到更好的结果。
- 难点不在 prompt 微调，而在 production infrastructure：persistence、sandboxing、credentials，以及让 agents 在大规模场景下持续运行。
- model 和 harness 正在深度耦合，所以那种“通用、可随时替换”的架构正在失去优势，model-specific 的 agent design 才更吃香。

Angela，Anthropic 里负责 Claude platform product 的负责人，和 Caitlin，engineering 负责人，讲的是一套更务实、没那么花哨的思路：把那些枯燥但关键的部分直接内建进去，让 model 更好用。他们认为，platform 应该继续演进成“whatever it’s like the set of primitives and infrastructure that enables you to basically get the outcome as fast as possible.” 这意味着 messages API、file systems、skills、code execution、web search、memory 和 managed infrastructure——不只是 token 的进出。

他们最直接的判断是，大多数团队都低估了痛点到底在哪。很多人以为 harness engineering 最难，但真正的墙通常出现在后面：“everyone hits an infrastructure wall.” agent 一旦能在 Mac mini 上跑通，或者在一个快速 prototype 里表现不错，到了 production 就会变成 uptime、state、storage、security 和 long-running jobs 的一团乱麻。这也是 Claude Managed Agents 存在的原因：Anthropic 把自己反复重建的东西，直接做成了产品。

他们还认为，过去那种“先做通用 harness，以后再换 model”的思路正在过时。随着 models 差异越来越大，最好的结果来自更有针对性地把 harness 和 model 配在一起。换句话说，platform 现在不再是中性的底层管道——它已经成了 model 行为的一部分，而这种路径依赖很重要。
